title: Refund handling walkthrough — Thursday 2026-10-08 (synthetic)

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: Thanks for joining. Kenji is new on the support team, so I'll walk through how we handle refund requests end to end.

transcript.speaker: Kenji
transcript.text: Great, I've only seen the ticket queue so far.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: Step one: the customer submits the refund form in the help widget. That creates a ticket tagged refund.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: Step two: the on-duty agent checks the order in the admin panel, mainly the order date and the amount.

transcript.speaker: Kenji
transcript.text: What are we checking for?

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: If the order is less than thirty days old and under fifty dollars, the agent approves it right away.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: If it's older than thirty days or over fifty dollars, the agent escalates the ticket to a team lead.

transcript.speaker: Omar
transcript.text: That's me or Rosa most weeks. The team lead looks at the customer history and either approves or rejects.

transcript.speaker: Kenji
transcript.text: And if the lead rejects it?

transcript.speaker: Omar
transcript.text: Then the agent replies with the rejection macro, which explains the policy and offers store credit instead.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: Once a refund is approved, by the agent or the lead, the agent marks the ticket approved and finance picks it up.

transcript.speaker: Omar
transcript.text: Finance issues the refund to the original payment method within five business days.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: The last step: when finance confirms, the customer gets the automatic refund-issued email and the ticket closes.

transcript.speaker: Kenji
transcript.text: How often do refunds get escalated?

transcript.speaker: Omar
transcript.text: Too often, honestly. Most escalations are orders between fifty and a hundred dollars, and we approve almost all of them.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: Yeah, the fifty dollar limit is old. Prices went up since we set it.

transcript.speaker: Omar
transcript.text: I'd raise the automatic approval limit to a hundred dollars.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: Agreed. Let's raise the automatic approval limit from fifty to one hundred dollars, starting today.

transcript.speaker: Kenji
transcript.text: So under a hundred dollars and under thirty days, I approve it myself.

transcript.speaker: Rosa
transcript.text: Exactly. Everything else still goes to a team lead.

transcript.speaker: Kenji
transcript.text: Makes sense. Thanks, this was really clear.

decisions: Raise the automatic refund approval limit from $50 to $100
